text:
mike: Kicking off onboarding for nubis-8b (community checkpoint). Legal flagged a clause about "derivative artifacts" and explicit attribution. Can we offer a 4-bit quantized serve-only variant without exposing binaries? :thinking:

tara: Paste the exact license excerpt please. small wording changes change the risk profile.

mike: Copied: ```
Redistribution: The model weights and any derivative binary artifacts (including quantized or otherwise transformed weight files) may not be redistributed for commercial purposes. Hosting the model for API inference is permitted provided the binaries are not publicly distributed. Attribution: Products using the model must credit the Original Authors and link to LICENSE.
```

elena: From ML experiments: ran 4-bit GPTQ and a 3-bit experimental run. 4-bit shows MMLU 61.8 -> 60.3 (-1.5), latency ~2.2x faster. 3-bit is smaller but MMLU -3.4 and hallucination up ~1.6%. Safety regressions small at 4-bit (FPR +0.3) but higher at 3-bit.

samir: Ops/infra: We must ensure no artifact download links, scrub any transient quant files in public buckets, and ensure backups don't create accessible copies. Also block any build that would mount binaries into customer-controlled VMs unless legal exception granted.

compliance-bot: Ingest scan: nubis-8b fp16 tarball found at s3://models/internal/nubis-8b/2026-03-23/; license tag NUB-1. No quant artifacts detected yet. Public ACL: false.

tara: Legal POV: wording explicitly calls out derivative binary artifacts. Quantized weights look covered. However the clause allows hosting for API inference so serve-only should be OK if binaries are never redistributed. Still need a short written memo from counsel to record interpretation.

mike: While legal drafts memo, ML: please run the full eval runbook (MMLU, HellaSwag, Summarization Rouge, Safety regression, embedding similarity) for the 4-bit build and upload diffs. If 4-bit is acceptable we can gate it to Hosted + Dedicated-serve-only with no-download policy.

elena: Will run full eval. Early embedding sims look good (mean cos sim 0.97 vs fp16). I'll also run prompt-level regression tests and flag any safety hotspots.

samir: I'll add a pipeline hook: deny_export when metadata.license=="NUB-1" and schedule a daily scrub for any artifacts in public buckets with that model tag. Also add audit log for any attempted access. PR pending.

ci-bot: Deployed branch "nubis/quant-eval" to staging-gpu-small; logs at https://ci.internal/builds/12045 :rocket:

compliance-bot: Counsel update: "Serve-only deployment is permitted under NUB-1 provided binaries (including quantized derivatives) are not redistributed. For Dedicated customer-hosted scenarios where the customer is given direct file access, obtain a signed exception prohibiting downstream redistribution or refuse binary access. Attribution required as described."

mike: Good. Action items: 1) Elena run full eval + upload diffs; 2) Samir implement deny_export hook & scrub job; 3) Tara record legal memo in compliance tracker and provide suggested attribution text; 4) Mike draft canary RFC for internal rollout (Hosted + Dedicated serve-only, no downloads, fp16 fallback route).

elena: Uploaded eval diffs: https://artifacts.internal/nubis-8b/evals/2026-03-23-4bit.csv  MMLU: base 62.1 -> 60.3, HellaSwag 85.6 -> 84.4, Rouge-L -1.3, Safety FPR +0.3, Embedding sim 0.97. I'll post prompt-level examples in the eval doc.

samir: PR posted: https://git.internal/infra/artifacts/+/623  adds metadata check to block downloads for license=NUB-1, schedules scrub job for public buckets, and restricts download roles to [security, compliance] only.

tara: Draft attribution: "Nubis-8B  Nubis Research Collective. Licensed under NUB-1. See LICENSE." Adding machine-readable provenance header: `X-Model-Provenance: nubis-8b;license=NUB-1;quantized=4bit;artifact_date=2026-03-23`. I'll drop the legal memo in the compliance tracker.

mike: Perfect. We'll proceed with an internal canary behind Hosted and Dedicated serve-only routes and keep fp16 fallback for sensitive endpoints. Leaving thread open until canary RFC merges. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
